title: What does the number beside each sweet tell us?
description: A teacher's table of sweets and tally marks has a number beside each sweet. The video reads two rows of tally marks, names the number as a frequency, and compares them, while Keeko doubts whether the frequency counts rows or children.
teaching_notes: One idea: the frequency of an item is the number of times it occurs, found by reading its tally marks. Watch for children who count the row of the item instead of the children who chose it.

source: The frequency table: what it tells and what it cannot
video_script.why: The child reads tally marks as a number and learns the name frequency for that number.
video_script.substitution: the jalebi and gulab jamun rows of the book's sweets table
video_script.anchor: Ruhee's table of sweets, tally marks and numbers of children
video_script.wrong_answer: the frequency of jalebi is one
video_script.wrong_move: counts the row of jalebi once instead of counting the children who chose it
video_script.payoff_line: The frequency of jalebi is six and of gulab jamun is nine, so more children chose gulab jamun.

final_answer.spoken: jalebi six and gulab jamun nine

names.Ruhee: teacher who buys sweets by the class preferences

never_show: the frequencies of gujiya, barfi and rasgulla
maths_rules: Jalebi: one bundle of 5 and 1 stroke, so 5 + 1 = 6.
Gulab jamun: one bundle of 5 and 4 strokes, so 5 + 4 = 9.
9 is larger than 6, so more children chose gulab jamun.
video_script.design: Two rows of the book's table: sweet, tally marks and an empty box for the number, filled as each row is read.

beats.on_screen: title card with two rows of a sweets table: jalebi and gulab jamun, each with tally marks and an empty box for the number

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the two rows
marks.rows: the tally marks of the two rows light up
marks.ask: a question mark lights up between the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a table from your book, made by Ruhee for a class.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Each sweet has a row of tally marks beside it.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these two sweets did more children choose?

beats.on_screen: the two rows and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a card names the empty column: the number of children who chose a sweet is its frequency; the whole table is a frequency table

marks.name: the word frequency is written above the column

narration: <bookmark mark='number'/>The number of children who choose a sweet is called its frequency.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A table that lists each sweet with its frequency is a frequency table.
We find each frequency by reading the tally marks.

beats.on_screen: Given: jalebi has one bundle and 1 stroke; gulab jamun has one bundle and 4 strokes

marks.given: the two tally rows are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, jalebi has one bundle and one stroke, and gulab jamun has one bundle and four strokes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the frequency of each sweet, and the sweet chosen by more children

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the frequency of each sweet and compare them.

marks.jalebi: the bundle is counted as five, one stroke is added and 6 is written in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='jalebi'/>Step one, read the tally for jalebi.
One bundle is five and one stroke is one, so the frequency is six.

marks.gulab: the bundle is counted as five, four strokes are added and 9 is written in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='gulab'/>Step two, read the tally for gulab jamun.
One bundle is five and four strokes are four, so the frequency is nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: compare the frequencies 9 and 6; 9 is the larger

marks.compare: the two frequencies are set side by side and the larger one is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='compare'/>Step three, compare the two frequencies. Nine is larger than six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: frequency of jalebi 6, gulab jamun 9; more children chose gulab jamun
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The frequency of jalebi is six and of gulab jamun is nine, so more children chose gulab jamun.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the word one written beside the jalebi row and crossed out, with the six children behind the row lit up

marks.doubt: the word one appears beside the jalebi row
marks.fix: the six children who chose jalebi light up and the word six replaces it

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the frequency of jalebi is one, because jalebi has only one row.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But frequency counts the children who chose a sweet, not the rows.
Six children chose jalebi, so its frequency is six.
